Seeth
sē´ĕth
v. (third person singular of see; rendering Hebrew ra'ah, Greek blepo and theoreo)
Old English sēon. The AV's third-person form of see, kept for the one verse the corpus most needs it in: the LORD seeth not as man seeth.

Biblical Definition

God seeth what man cannot. “The LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart” (1Sa 16:7). He “seeth under the whole heaven” (Job 28:24). Christ builds three commands on it: alms, prayer, and fasting are for “thy Father which seeth in secret” (Mat 6:4, 6, 18). The Son does “what he seeth the Father do” (John 5:19), and the world cannot receive the Spirit “because it seeth him not” (John 14:17). The elders in Ezekiel's vision say the opposite creed in the dark: “The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth” (Eze 8:12). John turns the word on the Christian: “whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?” (1Jn 3:17).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines see as to perceive by the eye; to observe; to discern; to understand; to attend or regard.

expand to see more

SEE, v.t. To perceive by the eye; to have knowledge of the existence and apparent qualities of objects by the organs of sight.

2. To observe; to note or notice; to know; to regard or look to.

3. To discover; to descry; to understand.

Key Scripture

1Sa 16:7 — "But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart."

Mat 6:4 — "That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly."

John 5:19 — "Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise."

1Jn 3:17 — "But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?"

Eze 8:12 — "Then said he unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The LORD seeth us not; the LORD hath forsaken the earth."

John 14:17 — "Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you."

Modern Corruption

God's seeing the heart is quoted as comfort for the unrepentant, when it was spoken to pass a man over.

expand to see more

“God knows my heart” is the modern use of 1 Samuel 16:7, and it is offered as an excuse: the conduct was poor, but the heart was good, and God sees the heart. The verse was spoken to disqualify Eliab. Samuel looked at the eldest son and was sure; the LORD looked at the heart and refused him. That God seeth the heart is the reason to fear, not the reason to relax — “the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I the LORD search the heart” (Jer 17:9–10). A man who appeals from his conduct to his heart has appealed to the harsher court.

Ezekiel 8 shows the practical atheism of religious men. Seventy elders of Israel stand in the dark with censers, every man in the chambers of his imagery, and their creed is one sentence: “The LORD seeth us not.” Every hidden sin is a small Ezekiel 8; it can only be done by first believing, for the length of the act, that God does not see. Matthew 6 turns the same fact into promise. The alms given, the prayer prayed, and the fast kept where no man sees are seen — “thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.” The one audience never misses a performance, and it is the only one that pays.

First John 3:17 forbids the spiritualising of the word. The man who seeth his brother have need and shuts up his bowels of compassion has seen, and seeing was the whole obligation. Love that has seen a need and done nothing is not love that is waiting for guidance; John asks how the love of God dwelleth in it at all.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew ra'ah (H7200), to see, look, regard; Greek blepo (G991), to look at; theoreo (G2334), to behold, perceive.

expand to see more

Hebrew ra'ah (H7200) — to see, regard; 1 Samuel 16:7, Job 28:24, Genesis 16:13, “Thou God seest me.”

Greek blepo (G991) — to look, see; Matthew 6:4, 6:6, 6:18, John 5:19.

Greek theoreo (G2334) — to behold, discern; John 14:17, 14:19, 1 John 3:17.

Usage

"“The LORD seeth not as man seeth” — Eliab passed over."

"“Thy Father which seeth in secret” — the audience of one."

"“The LORD seeth us not” — the elders' creed in the dark."
